modelsReviewed.summary: 29-day Senate general-election poll-margin model; 29–59 day source window; historical population labels/release clocks unavailable; not used for a different contract target.
45-day Senate general-election D–R final-margin error model, 45–75 day window; not extended outside scope.
45-day Governor general-election poll-margin model; not transported to late-October-field polling.

calibration.reason: The reviewed models estimate two-major-party vote-margin errors; current party-winner contracts need exact exhaustive candidate/settlement mapping and a scoped unconditional winner-probability bound. Known newer releases lack retained, hash-verified primary-source bytes.

exclusions.rule: A contract is eligible only when its exact market/office/stage/candidate settlement, primary source bytes/hash, existing scope-matched error model, numerical lower bound and captured offer all match. Poll percentages alone never become win probabilities.

priceVsBound.result: No defensible contract-level probability bound was available. For every captured quote, the report retains bid/ask, size, source age, and ask plus one adverse tick; lower-bound edge is null rather than inferred from poll share.

limitations: The Iowa Emerson October 9 release has poll shares and fieldwork dates in the task evidence but its primary page bytes were not retained locally; the source hash is therefore null and it is not used as a probability input.
The newer Texas Siena October 13 and New York Emerson October 8 source records are listed with null hashes; these are not used as probability inputs.
The local poll ledger is not a guarantee of exhaustive internet-wide poll discovery. Other market contracts are explicitly excluded where no exact verified primary source is in the captured ledger.
No poll share is treated as a probability. No uncalibrated horizon transport, national prior, complement assumption, or pollster average is added.
Captured book snapshots are display quotes only. No continuity, queue priority, actual fill, account state, order or profit is inferred.
This is an offline source/quote screen, not an execution or profitability finding.
